# The adversarial corpus for the guard's Tier 2 fail-safe (adr-42, iss-272).
#
# Every line is `<expectation>\t<command line>`. The expectations are:
#
#   quiet  the fail-safe must NOT fire. A hazard named inside a quoted argument,
#          inside a path, or as data is not a hazard.
#   warn   the fail-safe SHOULD fire. A hazard reached through a launcher the
#          wrapper table does not name — the class iss-272 recorded as silent.
#   block  Tier 1 matches at command position; Tier 2 never runs.
#   fp     the fail-safe fires and should not. These are ACCEPTED false
#          positives, pinned so the shape stays visible and a change in either
#          direction shows up in a diff rather than in the field.
#
# The `fp` lines are the whole cost of this design: unquoted hazard-shaped text
# in a command line where no entry matched. Quoting silences it. A reader who
# thinks that cost is too high should read the `warn` block first — that is what
# the cost buys.

# --- quiet: the hazard is data, not a command -------------------------------
quiet	echo 'do not run git push --force'
quiet	rg 'git push --force' docs/
quiet	git commit -m "ban git push --force"
quiet	gh issue create --title 'git push --force'
quiet	grep -rn "gh repo delete" .
quiet	printf '%s\n' "rm -rf /"
quiet	sed -i 's/git push --force/git push/' README.md
quiet	awk '/git push --force/ {print}' log.txt
quiet	python3 -c "print('git push --force')"
quiet	perl -e 'print "git push --force"'
quiet	cat notes/git-push-force.md
quiet	ls -la gh-repo-delete/
quiet	git log --grep 'git push --force'
quiet	echo "rm -rf is dangerous"
quiet	test -f scripts/gh-repo-delete.sh

# --- quiet: ordinary work, no hazard anywhere -------------------------------
quiet	make preflight
quiet	go test ./...
quiet	npm run build
quiet	docker ps -a
quiet	git status --short
quiet	kubectl get pods -A
quiet	terraform plan -out=tf.plan
quiet	rsync -av src/ dest/

# --- quiet: arithmetic and substitutions in everyday shapes -----------------
# An arithmetic expansion is an expression, not commands (review2-guard
# finding 5), and a substitution's output is an unknown word that fails closed
# only where it could be a hazard.
quiet	echo "$(( (1+2) * 3 ))"
quiet	echo $(( (1+2) * 3 ))
quiet	sleep "$(( 2 * 60 ))"
quiet	n=$(( n + 1 ))
quiet	git -C "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" status --short
quiet	git push -u origin "$(git branch --show-current)"
quiet	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && make build
quiet	export PATH="$(go env GOPATH)/bin:$PATH"

# --- block: the wrapper class iss-272 recorded as silent allows --------------
# Every one of these exited 0 with no output before adr-42. Part A made them loud
# warns without naming anything; part B named them, which upgrades the warn to a
# precise block. Both steps matter, and in that order: the warn is the safety
# property, the block is the precision, and the enumeration is only safe to be
# incomplete because the warn is underneath it.
block	nice git push --force origin main
block	nice -n 5 git push --force origin main
block	setsid git push --force origin main
block	flock /tmp/lock git push --force origin main
block	stdbuf -o0 git push --force origin main
block	chroot / git push --force origin main
block	ionice -c3 git push --force origin main
block	eatmydata git push --force origin main
block	busybox sh -c "gh repo delete owner/repo"
block	chrt -f 99 git push --force origin main
block	taskset -c 0 git push --force origin main
block	unshare -r git push --force origin main
block	nice -n 5 -- git push --force origin main

# --- warn: launchers no list would ever contain -----------------------------
warn	myrunner git push --force origin main
warn	parallel git push --force ::: a b
warn	watch -n1 git push --force origin main
warn	ssh host git push --force origin main
warn	docker run img git push --force origin main
warn	./deploy.sh git push --force origin main

# --- warn: git launches things too, which is why the gate is not argv[0] -----
warn	git bisect run git push --force origin main
warn	git submodule foreach git push --force origin main

# --- the per-segment gate, not a per-line one -------------------------------
# A per-line gate would let the matched git-clean disarm the fail-safe for
# everything after it — a one-token off switch. `nice` is enumerated now, so this
# resolves as a Tier 1 block; the same shape behind an UNENUMERATED launcher is
# the warn line below, and that is the case the gate actually protects.
block	git clean -fd ; nice git push --force origin main
warn	git clean -fd ; myrunner git push --force origin main

# --- block: Tier 1 still owns what it can see -------------------------------
block	git push --force origin main
block	sudo git push --force origin main
block	xargs -I{} git push --force origin {}
block	gh repo delete owner/repo
block	sh -c "git push --force origin main"

# --- block: the exec-string family, which speculation cannot reach ----------
# A command string run by a shell the carrying program is NOT. The payload is one
# opaque token, so no speculative start can see inside it; only the verb table
# reaches these. The long spellings are listed because a generalisation of the
# shell path would have resolved the short ones for free and silently allowed
# every one of these.
block	su -c "gh repo delete owner/repo"
block	su bob -c "gh repo delete owner/repo"
block	su --command "gh repo delete owner/repo"
block	su --command="gh repo delete owner/repo"
block	su --session-command "gh repo delete owner/repo"
block	runuser -c "git push --force origin main"
block	runuser --command "git push --force origin main"
block	script -c "git push --force origin main" /dev/null
block	script --command "git push --force origin main" /dev/null
block	flock /tmp/lock -c "git push --force origin main"
block	flock /tmp/lock --command "git push --force origin main"
block	su -s /bin/sh -c "gh repo delete owner/repo"
block	runuser -u bob -- git push --force origin main

# --- quiet: the same verbs doing ordinary work ------------------------------
quiet	su - bob
quiet	script /tmp/typescript
quiet	script -q /dev/null
quiet	flock /tmp/lock true
quiet	echo "su -c 'gh repo delete owner/repo'"

# --- quiet: a `-c` that belongs to the LAUNCHED command, not to the verb ------
# Verified against util-linux 2.39.3: `flock /tmp/lock /bin/echo -c "..."` prints
# its arguments, so nothing runs the string. Reading it as a payload was both a
# false block and — because the segment then looked understood — a one-token off
# switch for the fail-safe.
quiet	flock /tmp/lock /bin/echo -c "git push --force origin main"
quiet	flock -w 5 /tmp/lock /bin/echo --command "git push --force origin main"
warn	flock /tmp/lock kubectl exec -c app pod -- gh repo delete owner/repo

# --- fp: accepted false positives, and the exact shape they take ------------
fp	rg git push --force docs/
fp	grep -rn gh repo delete .
